rubric.evidence: Every claim traces to a primary source fetched live on 2026-07-26: Fetch Standard method steps (unusable → TypeError; null body → new closed empty ReadableStream; UTF-8 decoder 'regardless of the presence or the value of a Content-Type header … charset parameter'), FileAPI Blob steps and its readAsText() distinction note, Chromium body.idl/blob.idl bindings ([RuntimeEnabled=TextStreamMethod, RaisesException]), runtime_enabled_features.json5 (TextStreamMethod, status stable, crbug.com/514448226), and WPT textstream.any.js (bodyUsed true immediately; chunks are strings). Proposal maturity is stated precisely: whatwg/fetch PR #1862 is MERGED, so the spec text is normative — explicitly distinguished from listing status (Enabled by default) and detail status ('Proposed', updated 2026-06-22). An initial draft mis-stated the FileAPI readAsText() note (claimed readAsText always uses UTF-8); corrected before commit to the spec's actual point (readAsText accepts an encoding label; textStream has no encoding option).

Feature id 5146752165478400 appears in the v151 milestone listing under 'Enabled by default'; the route slug derives from the listing name per the documented slug rule; the H1 is the listing name verbatim (textContent unchanged by the <wbr> break hints). Listing status, detail status (Proposed, desktop+Android 151), and ship stage (intent 5, desktop_first 151) are presented as separate facts.

Six h2 sections: at-a-glance metadata, Syntax (normative IDL + Chromium bindings + member reference covering parameters, return value, exceptions, null-body behavior, encoding, bodyUsed side effect), Examples (live embed + reader-loop snippet), Browser compatibility (BCD-backed per-interface), Specifications, See also (WPT, crbug, IDL files, adjacent MDN TextDecoderStream clearly labelled adjacent).

The lede gives the mental model (byte-stream body → ReadableStream of UTF-8 strings; shorthand for a TextDecoderStream pipe, minus the footgun — the feature's own stated motivation). The member reference separates behavior classes: exception contract, null-body contract, always-UTF-8 contract, and the immediate bodyUsed side effect. Vendor positions (Safari Positive) are explicitly separated from shipped support (Safari not supported per BCD).

The embed is the identity-verified showcase streaming-text-reader concept (200, same chromestatus id 5146752165478400, target-behavior demo). The snippet uses the canonical getReader() loop shape from WPT textstream.any.js rather than for-await (broader engine compatibility), operates on a real fetch response, and notes the Blob/Request cases without placeholder accumulation or fabricated state.

Real BCD-backed table extended per review (Chrome 151; Chrome for Android and WebView Android/iOS mirrors; Edge mirror; Firefox and Safari not supported per BCD; Node.js 26.5.0; Deno explicitly unknown — no BCD entry), each BCD file linked separately. Baseline banner says 'Limited availability' honestly (linked webstatus.dev query returns no entry). Vendor signals are cited from the ChromeStatus API feature record (linked) — Firefox 'No signal', Safari 'Positive' framed as a recorded signal, not an official WebKit standards position for a feature this small — kept strictly separate from the BCD support rows. An earlier revision cited core_enums.py for per-feature vendor views; independent review rejected that provenance and it was removed from every page and the contract.

Direct primary-source link contract applied: every named source links separately to its canonical original — fetch.spec.whatwg.org#dom-body-textstream, w3c.github.io/FileAPI anchors (#dom-blob-textstream, #blob-get-stream, #failureReason), encoding.spec.whatwg.org#dom-textdecoderoptions-fatal, all four Chromium IDL/runtime files, both WPT test files, all three BCD files, the ChromeStatus API feature record and feature page, the webstatus.dev query URL, whatwg/fetch PR #1862, crbug.com/514448226, MDN TextDecoderStream (adjacent, labelled), and the three showcase routes (the visible 'chrome-platform-showcase' label is itself a link). All external links use target=_blank rel=noopener. Zero plain-text source labels.

Single main and h1; sequential h1→h2; four semantic tables with captions and scoped headers (row headers on reference rows, column headers on tabular data); banner role=note with aria-label; descriptive iframe title; first-column width hint (32%/7.5rem) keeps row labels wrapping at word boundaries at 390px.

Screenshot review caught a real mobile defect pre-commit: the H1's unbreakable token 'response/request/blob' clipped at 360px CSS width. Fixed with <wbr> break hints (textContent identical to the listing name); re-shot mobile confirms clean three-line wrap. Per-page responsive run + chrome-devtools-mcp matrix at 1280×800 and 390×844 verify no document-level horizontal overflow at either size; wide code blocks scroll internally by design (pre overflow-x auto), matching the accepted house pattern.

Iframe src is the feature's own stable showcase route (v151/textstream-for-response-request-blob/streaming-text-reader/), identity-matched to the same chromestatus id (5146752165478400) and HEAD-verified 200 alongside both sibling concepts (response-pipeline, feature-detect), which are linked in See also. No repointing, no forked platform assertions.
